## PROGRAMS OF GRADUATE STUDY IN THE BASIC BIOLOGICAL SCIENCES

The Division of the Biological Sciences offers variety of graduate programs leading to the Ph.D. degree: Graduate programs are offered under the aegis of divisional departments as well as interdepartmental committees composed of faculty members with a common interest in a broad but definable area of advanced study. Some programs are organized into larger groups called clusters, structure that provides cohesion across programs through shared retreats, common curriculum; and shared administrative duties A few programs offer unique training opportunities and are not organized into cluster. Joint programs also may be devised in other divisions of the university; such as with chemistry in the Division of the Physical Sciences and psychology in the Division of the Social Sciences. The fundamentals of graduate education in the division are not altered by these

The University's hallmark emphasis on interdisciplinary research and collaboration; coupled with access to the latest technology and to three major affiliated laboratories , offers the opportunity to enrich human life in Chicago and around the globe through basic, translational, and clinical research:

The of the programs is the creation and dissemination of fundamental knowledge of life processes and the education and of outstanding young scholars in these disciplines: To this end, the Division of the Biological Sciences has assembled a dedicated and talented faculty; strong in research and teaching, and has developed laboratory and other facilities of the first rank that allow the faculty and graduate students to pursue their at the highest level of excellence. goal training goals

The programs of study to the Ph.D degree are organized by cluster below: leading

Biomedical Sciences: Cancer, Immunology Microbiology and Molecular Metabolism and Nutrition

- The Committee on Cancer Biology
- The Committee on Molecular Metabolism and Nutrition
- The Committee on Immunology
- The Committee on Microbiology

Darwinian Sciences: Ecological, Integrative; and Evolutionary Biology

- The Department of and Evolution Ecology
- Graduate Program in Integrative Biology
- The Committee on Evolutionary Biology

Molecular Biosciences: Biochemistry; Genetics, and Cell and Developmental Biology

- Graduate Program in Biochemistry and Molecular Biophysics
- The Department of Human Genetics
- The Committee on Development, Regeneration; and Stem Cell Biology
- The Committee on Genetics, Genomics, and Systems Biology

Neuroscience: Computational Neuroscience, Neurobiology and Integrative Neuroscience

- Graduate Program in Cell and Molecular Biology
- The Committee on Computational Neuroscience
- The Committee on Neurobiology
- Program in Integrative Neuroscience (Psychology)

- The Department of Public Health Sciences (M.S. and Ph.D.)
- The Committee on Medical Physics
- Graduate Program in Biophysical Sciences (Joint with the Division of Physical Sciences)

## ADMISSION PROCEDURES

The following requirements and procedures apply to those students wishing to follow a course of study to the Doctor of Philosophy degree in the division. Students may apply to a single cluster and as many as four individual units indicating their choices in order of preference: According to their own schedules, the units to will communicate directly with the student as needed. Final decision letters are issued by the BSD Office of Graduate and Postdoctoral Affairs (OGPA). leading applied
